selection_rationale: CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II workload (no GPU needed). Plan REQ-20 target: AMD EPYC 7B13 64-core at <$0.35/hr; fallback any 36+ core EPYC at <$0.40/hr. Search returned 2 EPYC 7B13 offers: id=31639237 (Norway, machine_id 55891, 64 effective cores, 252 GB RAM, $0.2290/hr, reliability 0.9967, 406-day duration) and id=36215847 (Japan, machine_id 8487, 128 cores, 504 GB RAM, $0.2685/hr, reliability 0.9986, 97 days). Selected 31639237: this is the SAME physical machine (machine_id 55891, Norway, EPYC 7B13 64-core, public IP 141.0.85.200) that t0080 used for its CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II run with proven environment-setup procedure (uv 0.11 + Python 3.12-bookworm + neuron 8.2.7 + pymoo 0.6.1.6) and proven SSH connectivity through ssh*.vast.ai proxy. Microarchitecture identity to t0080-t0083 guarantees the t0083 Pareto warm-start and t0093 60-cell post-fix fingerprint are reproducible inside tolerance for the smoke gate (REQ-9). Cost projection: 14-16 h worst-case wall-clock (8-gen NSGA-II without HV plateau) * $0.2290/hr = $3.21-$3.66, leaving a $0.34-$0.79 buffer under the $4.00 hard cap; central case (HV plateau at gen 6-7) ~10-12h * $0.2290 = $2.29-$2.75. The Japan EPYC 7B13 alternative is 17% more expensive ($0.0395/hr more) for the same 64-core EPYC 7B13 silicon. The Italy Xeon E5-2699 v4 at $0.1851/hr is 19% cheaper raw, but per t0080's documented profile the Xeon (Broadwell, 2016) is ~1.5x slower per-core for NEURON than EPYC 7B13 (Zen 3, 2021); projected 14-16h becomes 21-24h, total $3.89-$4.45 — exceeds the $4.00 cap. Reliability 0.9967 sits below the spec's 5-24h threshold of 0.995 but above the 1-5h threshold of 0.98; the plan's CostWatchdogTermination + HVPlateauTermination both write per-generation checkpoints (results/data/hv_trajectory.json + results/data/all_evaluations.json union pattern from t0083), so a mid-run host failure costs at most one generation of work to recompute, and t0080 used this exact machine successfully. The single idle RTX PRO 4000 GPU is bundled but not used (gpu_verified=false; cpu_verified=true is the t0080-style success criterion).

ls -la /root/.no_auto_tmux
exit
' | ssh -tt ...), after which non-TTY 'ssh root@ssh4.vast.ai -p 24984 <cmd>' works for stdin-piped commands. The implementation step can SSH directly with 'ssh -i C:/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 24984 root@ssh4.vast.ai'. Public IP is 141.0.85.200 (same as t0080's instance 36137287 record on machine_id 55891) but direct SSH to that port (machine_dir_ssh_port 41999) does NOT accept the registered key; must go through ssh4.vast.ai:24984 proxy.
